question: Which of the following theories was propounded in Dadabhai Naoroji’s 1901 book Poverty and Un-British Rule in India? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Subsidiary Alliance Theory
Two Nation Theory
Doctrine of Lapse Theory
Drain of Wealth Theory
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Drain of Wealth Theory

Explanation:
Dadabhai Naoroji propounded the Drain of Wealth Theory in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901). According to this theory, Britain continuously drained India's wealth to England during colonial rule, leading to India's poverty. Naoroji estimated that about £8-10 crore was drained annually from India. This theory provides a fundamental analysis of British economic exploitation. Other options - Subsidiary Alliance (Lord Wellesley), Two Nation (Jinnah), Doctrine of Lapse (Lord Dalhousie) - are not related to this book.

☛ Year of publication → 1901
☛ Annual drain amount → £8-10 crore
☛ Title of Naoroji → Grand Old Man of India
☛ Naoroji's affiliation → Early nationalist leader
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सिद्धांत, दादाभाई नौरोजी की 1901 में प्रकाशित पुस्तक 'पावर्टी एंड अन-ब्रिटिश रूल इन इंडिया (Poverty and Un-British Rule in India)' में प्रतिपादित किया गया था? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 3)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है धन-निष्कासन सिद्धांत

Explanation:
दादाभाई नौरोजी ने अपनी पुस्तक 'पावर्टी एंड अन-ब्रिटिश रूल इन इंडिया' (1901) में धन-निष्कासन सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित किया। इस सिद्धांत के अनुसार, ब्रिटिश शासन के दौरान भारत का धन लगातार ब्रिटेन में स्थानांतरित किया गया, जिससे भारत की गरीबी बढ़ी। नौरोजी ने गणना की कि भारत से प्रतिवर्ष लगभग 8-10 करोड़ पाउंड का धन निष्कासन होता था। यह सिद्धांत ब्रिटिश आर्थिक शोषण का मूलभूत विश्लेषण प्रस्तुत करता है। अन्य विकल्प - सहायक गठबंधन (लॉर्ड वेलेजली), दो राष्ट्र (जिन्ना), व्यपगत (लॉर्ड डलहौजी) - इस पुस्तक से संबंधित नहीं हैं।

question: India’s First Five-Year Plan (FYP) was launched in which year? (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: 1951
1947
1956
1961
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1951

Explanation:
India's First Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951. It was implemented from 1951 to 1956. The primary focus of this plan was the agriculture sector, as the country was facing food shortages at that time. The plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model. Due to its success, food grain production increased significantly. Under this plan, multi-purpose projects like the Bhakra Nangal Dam were initiated. The growth rate achieved during the First Five-Year Plan was 3.6%, which was higher than the target of 2.1%.

☛ Main focus of First Five-Year Plan → Agriculture sector
☛ Model of First Five-Year Plan → Harrod-Domar Model

☛ Major project under First Five-Year Plan → Bhakra Nangal Dam

question: Which of the following is the outcome of Globalization in India's economy? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Outsourcing
Liberalisation
Privatisation
Nationalisation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Outsourcing

Explanation:
Globalization refers to the integration of world economies, leading to free flow of goods, services, capital, and technology. In India, a key outcome of globalization has been outsourcing, where companies transfer their services or production to lower-cost countries. India became a prime destination for IT and BPO services due to its skilled and cheap labor force, resulting in job creation, foreign exchange earnings, and rapid growth of the service sector. While liberalisation and privatisation are linked to 1991 economic reforms, the immediate impact of globalization was the expansion of outsourcing. Nationalisation is opposite to this process.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Most prominent impact of globalization in India → Growth of outsourcing industries
☛ Sector most benefited from outsourcing → Information Technology (IT) and BPO
☛ India's role in globalization process → Emerging as a service exporter
☛ Meaning of outsourcing → A company's non-core activities assigned to third party
☛ Relationship between globalization and outsourcing → Globalization enabled outsourcing
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा, भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था में वैश्वीकरण का परिणाम है? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 3)

निजीकरण
राष्ट्रीयकरण

Explanation:
वैश्वीकरण का अर्थ है विश्व की अर्थव्यवस्थाओं का एकीकरण, जिससे वस्तुओं, सेवाओं, पूंजी और प्रौद्योगिकी का मुक्त प्रवाह होता है। भारत में वैश्वीकरण का एक प्रमुख परिणाम बहिःस्रोतन (outsourcing) रहा है, जिसमें कंपनियां अपनी सेवाएं या उत्पादन कम लागत वाले देशों में स्थानांतरित करती हैं। भारत अपनी कुशल और सस्ती श्रम शक्ति के कारण आईटी और बीपीओ सेवाओं के लिए एक प्रमुख गंतव्य बन गया। इससे रोजगार सृजन, विदेशी मुद्रा आय और सेवा क्षेत्र का तीव्र विकास हुआ। हालांकि उदारीकरण और निजीकरण 1991 के आर्थिक सुधारों से जुड़े हैं, वैश्वीकरण का तात्कालिक प्रभाव बहिःस्रोतन का विस्तार था। राष्ट्रीयकरण इसके विपरीत है।

question: For which of the following was the industrial license not exempted during the 1991 reforms? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Coal
Alcohol
Steel
Food processing
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alcohol

Explanation:
During the 1991 economic reforms, industrial licensing was abolished for most industries, but some strategic and socially sensitive sectors continued to require licenses. Alcohol was one such industry that remained under licensing. Among the other options, Coal, Steel, and Food processing were all exempted from licensing in the 1991 reforms. This was part of the Industrial Policy 1991, which aimed at liberalizing the economy and removing bureaucratic controls.

question: When prices rise between 20% to 100% per annum or even more, it is termed as - (RRB JE CBT I (31/05/2019) Shift 3)
options: Running inflation
Trotting inflation
Hyperinflation
Creeping inflation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hyperinflation

Explanation:
When prices rise between 20% to 100% per annum or even more, it is termed Hyperinflation. This is an extreme form of inflation, usually caused by excessive money supply and severe supply shortages. During hyperinflation, people hoard goods to preserve purchasing power, further driving up prices. Creeping inflation involves a 2-3% annual price rise, Running inflation is 10-20%, Trotting inflation is up to 20%, while Hyperinflation exceeds 20% annually. Hyperinflation is highly damaging to the economy, eroding savings and disrupting normal economic activity.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Mildest form of inflation → Creeping inflation
☛ Most severe form of inflation → Hyperinflation
☛ Moderate form of inflation → Running inflation
☛ Price rise rate in hyperinflation → >20% per annum
☛ Price rise rate in creeping inflation → 2-3% per annum
question_hi: जब कीमतें प्रतिवर्ष 20% से 100% के बीच या इससे अधिक की दर से बढ़ती हैं, तो इसे क्या कहा जाता है? (RRB JE CBT I (31/05/2019) Shift 3)
options_hi: प्रचलित मुद्रास्फीति (Running inflation)
तेज मुद्रास्फीति (Trotting inflation)
बेलगाम मुद्रास्फीति (Hyperinflation)
मंद मुद्रास्फीति (Creeping inflation)
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है बेलगाम मुद्रास्फीति (Hyperinflation)

Explanation:
जब कीमतें प्रतिवर्ष 20% से 100% या उससे अधिक की दर से बढ़ती हैं, तो इसे बेलगाम मुद्रास्फीति कहा जाता है। यह मुद्रास्फीति का एक अत्यधिक रूप है, जो आमतौर पर मुद्रा के अत्यधिक मूल्यह्रास और आपूर्ति में भारी कमी के कारण होता है। इस स्थिति में लोग अपनी क्रय शक्ति बचाने के लिए वस्तुओं का अधिक संग्रह करते हैं, जिससे कीमतें और बढ़ जाती हैं। मंद मुद्रास्फीति में कीमतें 2-3% बढ़ती हैं, प्रचलित मुद्रास्फीति में 10-20%, और तेज मुद्रास्फीति में 20% तक, जबकि बेलगाम मुद्रास्फीति में 20% से अधिक वार्षिक वृद्धि होती है। यह अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए अत्यंत हानिकारक होती है।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ मुद्रास्फीति का सबसे गंभीर रूप → बेलगाम मुद्रास्फीति (Hyperinflation)

question: Why is biological magnification a health risk even with limited pesticide use? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Non-biodegradable pesticides are immediately excreted and do not persist
Pesticides affect only soil microorganisms, not higher organisms
Non-biodegradable pesticides accumulate at successive trophic levels
The toxicity of pesticides decreases as they move up the food chain
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Non-biodegradable pesticides accumulate at successive trophic levels

Explanation:
Biological magnification is a process where non-biodegradable pesticides like DDT enter the food chain and increase in concentration at each trophic level. These chemicals persist in the environment and accumulate in organisms because they are not excreted. Even with limited use, the concentration becomes extremely high at higher trophic levels, such as in fish-eating birds. This can lead to reproductive failure, immune suppression, and reduced biodiversity. It poses a health risk because humans, as top consumers, can be affected by the accumulated toxins. The pesticides are not immediately excreted but stored in fatty tissues, leading to long-term exposure and health issues like cancer and hormonal disruptions.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Common example of biological magnification? → Accumulation of DDT in aquatic food chains
☛ Where is DDT concentration highest? → In top consumers like fish-eating birds
☛ What type of substances undergo biological magnification? → Non-biodegradable and toxic chemical compounds
☛ Effect of biological magnification on human health? → Risk of chronic toxicity, cancer, and hormonal imbalance

question:
Which statement correctly explains the role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
(RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: They recycle nutrients by breaking down dead organisms into simple substances
They convert inorganic substances into complex organic compounds
They directly provide food to carnivores
They absorb sunlight to produce energy-rich compounds
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is They recycle nutrients by breaking down dead organisms into simple substances

Explanation:
Decomposers play a vital role in an ecosystem by breaking down dead plants and animals into simple inorganic substances. This process releases nutrients back into the soil, making them available for producers. Decomposers like bacteria and fungi are essential for nutrient cycling. They do not perform photosynthesis, nor do they provide food directly to carnivores. Instead, they are saprophytes that feed on dead matter. By decomposing organic material, they prevent waste accumulation and maintain ecological balance. Thus, they ensure the continuous flow of nutrients in the ecosystem.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Main function of decomposers → Break down dead organisms into simple substances and recycle nutrients
☛ Examples of decomposers → Bacteria and fungi
☛ Type of nutrition in decomposers → Saprophytic nutrition
☛ Who makes energy from sunlight in ecosystem → Producers (green plants)
☛ Who makes complex organic compounds → Producers

question:
If decomposers were removed from an ecosystem, what would be the most immediate consequence?
(RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Rapid increase in herbivore population
Decrease in sunlight reaching producers
Increased plant growth due to more dead organic matter
Accumulation of waste and dead matter, disrupting nutrient cycling
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Accumulation of waste and dead matter, disrupting nutrient cycling

Explanation:
Decomposers (like bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic matter into simple nutrients, which are then reused by producers (plants). If decomposers are removed, dead bodies, leaves, and waste will accumulate, and nutrient cycling will stop. Plants will not get essential nutrients, affecting their growth. An increase in herbivore population or decrease in sunlight is not an immediate consequence. Disruption of nutrient cycling affects all trophic levels in the ecosystem, leading to long-term collapse.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Nutrient cycling in an ecosystem depends on? → Decomposers
☛ Examples of decomposers? → Bacteria, fungi, and earthworms
☛ What happens if decomposers are absent? → Dead matter accumulates and nutrient cycling stops
☛ How do producers obtain nutrients? → From soil, which is recycled by decomposers

question:
Which of the following combinations best explains why waste generation has become a major environmental issue in modern societies?
(RRB Technician Grade III (10/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Government regulations that limit the collection of biodegradable waste and its recycling
Increased use of biodegradable materials and better disposal habits
Reduced use of packaging materials and enhanced recycling
Improved lifestyles leading to more disposable and non-biodegradable materials
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Improved lifestyles leading to more disposable and non-biodegradable materials

Explanation:
Waste generation has become a major environmental issue in modern societies primarily due to improved lifestyles that lead to increased use of disposable and non-biodegradable materials. These materials do not decompose easily, causing pollution and filling up landfills. Government regulations aim to improve waste management, not limit collection of biodegradable waste. Increased use of biodegradable materials and better disposal habits would actually reduce the problem, not cause it. Reducing packaging and enhancing recycling are solutions, not causes. Therefore, the key reason is the shift in lifestyle towards convenience, resulting in more disposable and non-biodegradable waste that persists in the environment.

☛ Landfill problem → Non-biodegradable waste occupies space for long periods
☛ 3R principle of waste management → Reduce, Reuse, Recycle

question: Even though people eat different types of food, they may still absorb harmful chemical residues. This is because ____________. (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Food grains absorb only useful chemicals from soil
All plants produce natural pesticides
Chemicals persist and accumulate via biomagnification
Pesticides are completely destroyed during cooking
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chemicals persist and accumulate via biomagnification

Explanation:
Chemical residues like pesticides persist in soil and water, and enter the food chain through plants. Through biomagnification, these chemicals increase in concentration at each trophic level. Even if people consume different types of food, the chemicals have already been absorbed by plants and then passed on to herbivores and carnivores. Therefore, harmful residues accumulate in the bodies of organisms, including humans, regardless of dietary choices. Cooking does not completely destroy these persistent chemicals, and only useful chemicals are not absorbed selectively.

☛ What causes biomagnification? → Non-degradable and fat-soluble nature of chemicals
☛ What is a synonym of biomagnification? → Increase in maximum permissible concentration (MPC)

question: When chemicals such as pesticides enter food chains and get more concentrated at higher levels, the process is known as ____. (RRB Paramedical (13/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Biodegradation
Photosynthesis
Eutrophication
Biological magnification
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Biological magnification

Explanation:
Biological magnification is the process where toxic chemicals like pesticides enter a food chain and become more concentrated at each successive trophic level. These chemicals are not biodegradable and accumulate in the tissues of organisms. The concentration increases as they move up the food chain, causing the highest harm to top predators. This occurs in both aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. A classic example is DDT biomagnification leading to thinning of eggshells in birds.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is biological magnification? → Increase in concentration of toxic substances at each trophic level in a food chain.
☛ Cause of biological magnification → Non-biodegradable nature and fat solubility of chemicals.
☛ Famous example → DDT magnification in birds.
☛ Highest concentration found in? → Top trophic level organisms.
☛ Related process → Bioaccumulation (in one organism) vs biomagnification (along food chain).
question_hi: जब पीड़कनाशी जैसे रसायन खाद्य श्रृंखलाओं में प्रवेश करते हैं और उच्च स्तर पर अधिक सांद्रित हो जाते हैं, तो इस प्रक्रिया को ________ के रूप में जाना जाता है। (RRB Paramedical (13/03/2026) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following can happen when non-biodegradable waste is dumped into water bodies? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: It pollutes the water and harms aquatic life.
It helps aquatic plants grow.
It cleans the water.
It quickly dissolves in water.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It pollutes the water and harms aquatic life.

Explanation:
Non-biodegradable waste consists of materials like plastic, glass, and metals that do not decompose naturally. When such waste is dumped into water bodies, it remains there for a long time and pollutes the water. This waste harms aquatic life as animals may ingest it or get entangled, leading to injury or death. It does not dissolve quickly and does not clean the water. Instead, it reduces water quality and disrupts the ecosystem. It does not help aquatic plants grow; in fact, it hinders their growth by blocking sunlight and releasing toxins. Therefore, option 1 is correct.

☛ Example of biodegradable waste → Food waste, paper
☛ Main cause of water pollution → Dumping non-biodegradable waste
☛ Effect on aquatic life → Death due to ingestion or entanglement
☛ Result of waste in water bodies → Water pollution, loss of biodiversity

question: In a school canteen, students notice that many plastic cups and plates are thrown away daily. To solve this problem, they suggest switching to steel plates and reusable water bottles. This action mainly promotes ________. (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: More plastic recycling
Faster waste collection
Better packaging design
Reduction and reuse of waste
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Reduction and reuse of waste

Explanation:
This action primarily promotes waste reduction and reuse by replacing disposable plastic cups and plates with steel plates and reusable water bottles. It aligns with the principle of sustainable consumption, reducing the amount of waste generated. Unlike recycling, which processes waste after it is created, this approach prevents waste at the source. It also supports SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). The step does not focus on faster waste collection or better packaging design; instead, it encourages a shift toward durable, reusable alternatives. This reduces the environmental impact associated with single-use plastics and promotes a circular economy.

☛ Sustainable Development Goal 12 → Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns

question: Which distinguishing feature primarily differentiates a biosphere reserve from a national park in India, as per conservation and management objectives? (RRB Technician Grade III (10/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Biosphere Reserves (BRs) allow research, tourism, and local livelihoods in designated buffer and transition zones.
Biosphere Reserves (BRs) covers a smaller geographical area than national parks.
Biosphere Reserves (BRs) focuses exclusively on protection of wild animals.
Biosphere Reserves (BRs) does not aim at conservation of biological diversity.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Biosphere Reserves (BRs) allow research, tourism, and local livelihoods in designated buffer and transition zones.

Explanation:
Biosphere Reserves (BRs) and National Parks (NPs) are both protected areas, but their management objectives differ. National Parks primarily focus on wildlife conservation with limited human activities. In contrast, Biosphere Reserves have three zones: core, buffer, and transition. The buffer and transition zones permit scientific research, tourism, and livelihood activities for local communities. This promotes sustainable development while conserving biodiversity. Therefore, this feature—allowing human activities in designated zones—distinguishes a biosphere reserve from a national park in India.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What is the main objective of a National Park? → Wildlife conservation
☛ Which organization conceptualized Biosphere Reserves? → UNESCO
☛ Which was the first Biosphere Reserve in India? → Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
☛ In which zone of a Biosphere Reserve is tourism allowed? → Buffer and transition zones

question: Why is it important to dry agricultural produce first in sunlight and then in shade before storage? (RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 2)
options: To reduce moisture content and prevent growth of pests and fungi.
To improve the color and taste of the produce.
To increase the size and brightness of the grains.
To make the grains easier to pack and prevent growth of weeds.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To reduce moisture content and prevent growth of pests and fungi.

Explanation:
Agricultural produce contains high moisture, which encourages the growth of pests and fungi during storage, leading to spoilage. Drying in sunlight evaporates moisture, but intense heat may crack grains or degrade nutrients. Therefore, shade drying regulates temperature and maintains quality. This process reduces moisture to safe levels (about 12-14%), inhibiting microbial activity and prolonging storage life. This traditional method is cost-effective and widely used in post-harvest management.

question: How do check-dams help in improving agricultural water availability and soil quality? (RRB JE (25/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: They increase groundwater levels and reduce soil erosion.
They directly irrigate fields with river water and increase soil erosion.
They store water only for city use, and reduce soil erosion.
They divert water away from farms and increase soil erosion.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is They increase groundwater levels and reduce soil erosion.

Explanation:
Check-dams are small barriers built across streams or gullies to slow down water flow. This allows water to percolate into the ground, thereby increasing groundwater levels, which enhances water availability for agriculture. Additionally, by reducing the velocity of water, check-dams significantly decrease soil erosion, preserving fertile topsoil. They are an effective method of water conservation and soil management, especially in dry and semi-arid regions. Check-dams also help in flood control and recharge aquifers, making them a sustainable solution for improving agricultural productivity.

question: Why are crops with different nutrient requirements chosen for inter-cropping? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: To ensure maximum utilisation of nutrients supplied to the field
To increase the duration of crop growth
To prevent all pests and diseases completely
To allow for crop rotation in succession
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To ensure maximum utilisation of nutrients supplied to the field

Explanation:
In inter-cropping, crops with different nutrient requirements are chosen to ensure maximum and efficient utilisation of available nutrients in the soil. Growing crops with similar nutrient needs together can lead to deficiency of a particular nutrient, whereas crops with different requirements absorb different nutrients from the soil, maintaining nutrient balance and reducing wastage. This technique helps in increasing crop productivity and sustaining soil fertility. It also aids in pest and disease management by breaking the lifecycle of specific pests.

question:
Coal is primarily formed from:
(RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 1)
options: Remains of animals preserved in rocks
Lava flows from volcanoes
Mineral deposits in the Earth
Layers of dead plants compressed over millions of years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Layers of dead plants compressed over millions of years

Explanation:
Coal is a fossil fuel formed millions of years ago from the accumulation of dead plants in swampy areas. Layers of plants were buried under sediment and water, increasing pressure and temperature, initiating the process of carbonization. First peat forms, then lignite, bituminous coal, and finally anthracite. Coal has a high carbon content, making it a vital energy source.

question:
Refer to the two statements given below and choose the CORRECT option.

Statement A: Milch animals are reared primarily for the production of milk.

Statement B: Milch animals are mainly used for ploughing agricultural fields. (RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: Statement A is correct but B is incorrect.
Both statements A and B are incorrect.
Statement A is incorrect but B is correct.
Both statements A and B are correct.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Statement A is correct but B is incorrect

Explanation:
Milch animals are those raised primarily for milk production, such as cows, buffaloes, and goats. They form the basis of the dairy industry, producing milk which is processed into curd, cheese, butter, etc. On the other hand, for ploughing agricultural fields, draught animals like oxen, horses, and donkeys are used, which provide muscle power. Milch animals are not used for ploughing as they are not bred for that purpose. Thus, Statement A is correct, while Statement B is incorrect.

question: Crop rotation helps in controlling _______ by changing the type of crops grown in a pre-planned succession. (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: weeds and pests
over-irrigation
sunlight exposure
excess rainfall
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is weeds and pests

Explanation:
Crop rotation is an agricultural practice where different types of crops are grown in a planned sequence. It helps control weeds and pests by disrupting their life cycles, as they often depend on a specific crop. For instance, legumes fix nitrogen, improving soil fertility, while deep-rooted crops enhance soil structure. This method also prevents soil erosion and maintains nutrient balance. By reducing reliance on chemical pesticides, it is environmentally friendly. Thus, crop rotation effectively manages weed and pest populations.

☛ Which practice disrupts the life cycle of pests? → Crop rotation
☛ How many years is a typical crop rotation cycle? → Usually 3-4 years

question: Which of the following is NOT a non-renewable resource?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Natural Gas
Solar Energy
Liquefied Petroleum Gas
Coal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Solar Energy

Explanation:
Non-renewable resources are those that are available in limited quantities and cannot be replenished once used. Natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas, and coal are all fossil fuels that took millions of years to form and have finite reserves. Solar energy comes from the sun, which is abundant and continuously available, making it a renewable resource. It can be replenished naturally and is environmentally friendly. Thus, solar energy is not a non-renewable resource.
